summary: Neo Ensemble's chorus: Min Delay and Mod Depth (the sweep from Min Delay to Min Delay + 2 × Mod Depth) land on the sweep's geometric centre and its octaves, Fatness on the voices (four at most) and on a crossfade and output gain that keep FSM's fixed 1 : 2.5 dry-to-wet balance, Stereo on Spread.

rules.why: FSM Chorus2's delay is Min Delay + Mod Depth × (1 + sin), straight in samples: 2 + 1120.5 × value ÷ 240 for Min Delay (its display says 1102.5, hence × 1.0163) and 110.25 × value ÷ 240 for Mod Depth. Neo Ensemble sweeps in octaves round its Delay: the same ends.
FSM moves the right channel's taps Stereo ÷ taps on from the left's; Neo Ensemble moves its right voices Spread ÷ voices on: the same, in degrees.
FSM's taps; Neo Ensemble has four voices at most.

FSM mixes the dry signal at 1 ÷ 3.5 and each of its n taps at 2.5 ÷ (3.5·n); Neo Ensemble averages its voices times √voices: mix m with m ÷ (1 − m) = 2.5 ÷ √n gives each voice and the dry the same weights (n ≤ 4; above, the same wet power).
The output gain that puts the dry at 1 ÷ 3.5: (1 ÷ 3.5) ÷ (1 − m).

remarks: FSM Chorus2 sets its taps 60° apart on the LFO (whatever their number), Neo Ensemble its voices evenly round the cycle: with two to five taps the voices sit differently, so the chorus moves differently while its ends and levels match.
FSM Chorus2 counts its delays in samples, so its times change with the sample rate; the mapping reads them at 44.1 kHz, as its manifest does.
FSM Chorus2 has no feedback and no tone control: Neo Ensemble's are off and open.
